claim: Every tested model degrades on every main task under SHARDED, with 39% average degradation.

claim: CONCAT largely preserves FULL performance, supporting information preservation under rephrased shards.

comparison: CONCAT versus FULL.

author_interpretation: SHARDED loss is not explained by information loss in the shard wording.

claim: Stronger models get lost at a similar relative rate to weaker models.

claim: The average degradation is dominated by unreliability rather than aptitude loss.

comparison: FULL versus SHARDED.
statistical_method: Per-instruction 90th percentile and 90th-minus-10th percentile range, averaged across corpora.
author_interpretation: Lost in Conversation is principally a reliability phenomenon.

claim: The main effect appears once instructions span two or more turns in the gradual experiment.
value: Both GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini show a large reliability increase from two shards onward.
comparison: One through eight shards.
statistical_method: 10 simulations per instruction/model; 31 claimed source instructions expanded to 248 variants, though Appendix L contains a conflicting 'eight instructions' sentence.
author_interpretation: Providing everything at once is the only tested granularity that restores reliability.

claim: Later first answer attempts are associated with higher performance on Code and Math.

author_interpretation: Premature answer attempts can plant incorrect assumptions.

claim: Answer attempts grow longer over turns and remain longer even when correct.
value: Final SHARDED attempts are 20-300% longer; correct Code is 27% longer and correct Database is 14% longer than FULL.

statistical_method: Mean extracted-answer character length by attempt index; filtered correct subset for Code/Database.
author_interpretation: Models retain invalid assumptions and bloat later solutions.

author_interpretation: Loss-in-the-middle also occurs across conversation turns.
